stem:
Tatenda Moyo runs a wholesale grocery business in Masvingo. He keeps a three-column cash book and an analysed petty cash book on the imprest system (imprest US\$200, analysis columns: postage, cleaning, travel). On 1 April 2025 his cash book showed cash in hand US\$415 and cash at bank US\$3,870.

**Transactions for April 2025**

| Date | Transaction |
| --- | --- |
| 2 Apr | Received a cheque from Rufaro Store in settlement of its account of US\$2,740, less 5% cash discount |
| 4 Apr | Paid Gweru Millers US\$3,460 owed, less 4% cash discount, by bank transfer |
| 6 Apr | Cash sales US\$1,385 |
| 8 Apr | Paid US\$1,175 cash into the bank |
| 10 Apr | Kudzi Shop paid US\$867 cash in full settlement of US\$885 |
| 11 Apr | Paid wages in cash US\$565 |
| 12 Apr | Paid Bulawayo Oils by cheque US\$1,935 in full settlement of US\$1,980 |
| 15 Apr | Card sales US\$2,235 |
| 20 Apr | Paid rent online US\$975 |
| 30 Apr | Restored the petty cash imprest by bank transfer |

**Petty cash vouchers for April 2025**

| Date | Details | Voucher | US\$ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 3 Apr | Postage stamps | 71 | 13.40 |
| 5 Apr | Cleaning materials | 72 | 24.60 |
| 7 Apr | Bus fares | 73 | 16 |
| 9 Apr | Courier | 74 | 30 |
| 15 Apr | Cleaner's wages | 75 | 38 |
| 25 Apr | Taxi fare | 76 | 36 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the total of the discount allowed column for April.
parts.explanation: Rufaro Store $2,740 \times 5\% = 137$; Kudzi Shop $885 - 867 = 18$. Total US\$155.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Rufaro Store $2,740 \times 5\% = 137$; Kudzi Shop $885 - 867 = 18$. Total US\$155.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total of the discount received column for April.
parts.explanation: Gweru Millers $3,460 \times 4\% = 138.40$; Bulawayo Oils $1,980 - 1,935 = 45$. Total US\$183.40.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Gweru Millers $3,460 \times 4\% = 138.40$; Bulawayo Oils $1,980 - 1,935 = 45$. Total US\$183.40.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the total of the postage column of the petty cash book for April.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount transferred from the bank on 30 April to restore the petty cash imprest.
parts.explanation: Vouchers $13.40 + 24.60 + 16 + 30 + 38 + 36 = 158$. Cash left $200 - 158 = 42$; the amount to restore the imprest is $200 - 42 = 158$.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Vouchers $13.40 + 24.60 + 16 + 30 + 38 + 36 = 158$. Cash left $200 - 158 = 42$; the amount to restore the imprest is $200 - 42 = 158$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash balance at 30 April 2025.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the bank balance at 30 April 2025.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Prepare Tatenda's three-column cash book for April 2025. Balance the cash and bank columns and bring down the balances on 1 May 2025.

points.description: Opening balances 415 cash and 3,870 bank on the debit side
Rufaro Store: discount 137 and bank 2,603; Kudzi Shop: discount 18 and cash 867 (debit side)
Cash sales 1,385 in the cash column and card sales 2,235 in the bank column (debit side)

Contra 1,175 on both sides marked C; wages 565 (cash), rent 975 and petty cash 158 (bank) on the credit side
Balances c/d 927 cash and 3,493.40 bank; totals 2,667 and 9,883; balances b/d on 1 May

parts.explanation: Receipts and discount allowed on the debit side; payments and discount received on the credit side; contras on both sides.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: How is the total of the discount allowed column posted in Tatenda's ledger?

options.content: Debit the discount allowed account US\$155
options.rationale: Correct: discount allowed is an expense.

options.content: Credit the discount allowed account US\$155
options.rationale: The customers are credited individually; the total is debited.

options.content: Debit the discount received account US\$155
options.rationale: The debit column holds discounts allowed to customers.

options.content: Credit the trade receivables account US\$155
options.rationale: Each customer is credited with their own discount, not with the total.

parts.explanation: Debit discount allowed with the column total; customers have already been credited individually.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Explain how the imprest system helps Tatenda to control his petty cash.

points.description: Only a fixed, small amount (US\$200) is held, and it is restored only by the amount spent as shown by vouchers
Cash plus vouchers must always equal the imprest, so any shortage is found at a check

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The petty cashier holds only US\$200 and is reimbursed for exactly what the authorised vouchers show. At any time the cash plus the vouchers must equal US\$200, so a shortage is quickly detected.

parts.explanation: The fixed float and the voucher check give control.

explanation: A ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question on the three-column cash book (Form 2) and the petty cash book on the imprest system.
hints: Cash discount = amount owed − amount paid.
The petty cash restoration is a bank payment equal to the vouchers for the month.
Balance cash and bank separately; total the discount columns.
